m:parlament: It can only be visited on a guided tour, about 45 minutes long. Ticket from 1 January 2026: 7,000 Ft (about €19) for EU/EEA citizens, 14,000 Ft for others; reduced 3,500 Ft for EU students aged 6–24; under 6 free (official website parlament.hu). Buy online at jegymester.hu/parlament; you'll need ID. Open every day from 8am to 6pm until 31 October and from 8am to 4pm from 1 November. In weeks with parliamentary sessions, visits are limited on the first day (building open 8–10am, ticket office open until 11am) and it may close for official events: check the website. According to one guide it's closed on 23 October, 1 November and from 24 to 26 December (to be checked). Security checks take 20–30 minutes: arrive early. The «Shoes on the Danube» is a place of remembrance, not a backdrop for selfies.
m:halasz: Bastion: the lower terraces and the promenade are always open and free; the upper gallery costs 1,700 Ft (850 Ft reduced) and the «Panorama» ticket with the Mary Magdalene tower 2,700 Ft. The ticket desk is open 9am–7pm until 23 December (9am–9pm June to September), cards only; the Bastion is also free on 23 October and from 24 to 31 December (guide updated 3 October 2026, to be checked). Matthias Church: 3,400 Ft for the church, 4,000 Ft for the tower in time slots (matyas-templom.hu); it usually opens at 9am and closes around 5pm, but may close for masses and ceremonies (on Sundays it usually opens in the afternoon: check the website). The funicular from the Danube is listed as closed from 5 to 16 October 2026. Other ways up: bus 16 from Deák Ferenc tér or the steps from Clark Ádám tér (about 10 minutes).
m:szechenyi: 2026 prices from the official website: day ticket with locker 13,200 Ft (about €36) Monday to Thursday, 14,800 Ft Friday and weekends, 15,800 Ft on public holidays and in high season; the «Good Morning Budapest» ticket (entry by 9am) costs 10,500 Ft Monday to Thursday. A cabin costs 1,000 Ft extra. Hours: Monday–Thursday 7am–8pm, Friday 7am–10pm, Saturday and Sunday 8am–8pm; the pools close 20 minutes earlier and the ticket desks an hour earlier. Book online at tickets.szechenyibath.hu; the automatic ticket machines take cards only. Bring a swimsuit, flip-flops and a towel (not for hire); a swimming cap is only needed in the lap pool. Entry from age 14 only. The historic Gellért bath is closed for a long renovation.
m:basilica: Hours and prices not checked on the official website (bazilika.biz): guides give very different figures, so check before you go. According to an April 2026 guide the church is open Monday to Friday 9am–5pm, Saturday 9am–1pm and Sunday 1–5pm; the dome terrace has a separate ticket, usually open 10am–5:30pm in April, May and October and until 4:30pm from November to March. Masses, weddings and concerts may limit entry. Shoulders and knees must be covered; no food or drink inside.
m:lanchid: Free to walk at any hour: in the evening the bridge and the Castle are lit up. The Castle funicular (Sikló) leaves from Clark Ádám tér: about 5,000 Ft return (August 2026 guide, to be checked), with its own ticket, not the BKK one. It's listed as closed from 5 to 16 October 2026. Alternatively walk up in about 10 minutes or take bus 16.
m:dohany: Always closed on Saturdays and Jewish holidays. Hours from the official website jewishtourhungary.com: in October Sunday–Thursday 10am–6pm (last entry 5pm) and Friday 10am–4pm (last entry 3pm); from 2 November Sunday–Thursday 10am–4pm and Friday 10am–2pm. Closed on 1 November and 24 and 25 December. The 45-minute guided tour is included, also in Italian. I didn't read the price on the official website: guides give figures between about 9,000 and 14,500 Ft (€25–40), check first. Shoulders and knees must be covered, and men cover their heads (a kippah is provided at the entrance). Online tickets have a fast lane.
m:mercato: Entry is free. Hours from two 2026 guides: Monday–Friday 6am–6pm, Saturday 6am–4pm, Sunday 10am–4pm (an English page from the operator still lists Sunday as closed: check). Closed on public holidays, including 23 October and 1 November 2026. Upstairs, according to an October 2026 guide, the Fakanál restaurant has goulash soup at about 3,100 Ft and pork stew with dumplings at about 5,100 Ft. The paprika aisle is the most expensive: stalls inside the market are often cheaper.
m:gellert: The walk is free and always open. Walk up in about 20 minutes from Szent Gellért tér or Liberty Bridge, on uphill paths: comfortable shoes. The Gellért bath, at the foot of the hill, is closed for a long renovation (until 2028 according to one guide).
m:hosok: The square, the park and the outside of the castle are free and always open. The yellow M1 metro, the city's oldest line (1896), runs under Andrássy út to Hősök tere and the Széchenyi Baths, in about 15 minutes from Deák Ferenc tér. The museums around the square have their own hours and closures: I didn't check them on their websites, check before going.
m:margit: The island is free and always open. From the centre take tram 4 or 6 to Margaret Bridge (Margit híd) or tram 2 to Jászai Mari tér, then walk across the bridge (about 5 minutes). I didn't check the hours of the musical fountain and the bike rentals: check on site.
vd:gerbeaud: The historic pâtisserie on Pest's main square, open since 1858: rooms with mirrors and decorated ceilings, a big cake display and the traditional Dobos, the layered cake with caramel glaze. Have a coffee with a slice and watch the square.
vp:gerbeaud: A coffee with a slice of cake is around 4,500–6,500 Ft (€12–18) (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:kor: A neighbourhood bistro a short walk from the Basilica, with a menu of Hungarian home cooking that changes with the seasons: soups, meat stews with nokedli dumplings and desserts. Small and often full at lunch and dinner.
vp:kor: A main course is around 5,500–8,500 Ft (€15–23) (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed (it appears to be closed on Sundays).
vd:hungarikum: A restaurant near Parliament serving only classic Hungarian dishes: goulash, meat pörkölt with dumplings, chicken paprikás, cakes and Hungarian wine. Simple cooking and generous portions, in a tidy setting.
vp:hungarikum: A main course is around 5,500–9,000 Ft (€15–25) (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:central: A Belle Époque literary café near Ferenciek tere, reopened in 2000 in the historic building: Hungarian breakfasts, cakes and simple dishes in a high-ceilinged room with banquettes.
vp:central: A coffee with a cake is around 4,500–6,500 Ft and a dish about 6,000–9,000 Ft (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:ruszwurm: Budapest's oldest pâtisserie, since 1827, in a small Biedermeier room a short walk from Matthias Church: krémes, the Buda cream cake, Dobos and Esterházy. Little space, so in high season there's a queue.
vp:ruszwurm: A coffee with a slice is around 3,000–4,500 Ft (€8–12) (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:karavan: A courtyard in the Jewish quarter with street food stalls: lángos, the fried flatbread with sour cream, garlic and cheese, grilled meat sandwiches, kürtőskalács, the spiral cake. Sit at the outdoor tables and pick whichever stall you like.
vp:karavan: A street food dish is around 3,000–5,500 Ft (€8–15) (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed: in winter some stalls close.
vd:menza: A restaurant with 1970s décor on the café square near Oktogon: modern Hungarian cooking with goulash, chicken paprikás, soups and desserts like somlói galuska, the sponge dessert with cream and chocolate.
vp:menza: A main course is around 5,000–8,000 Ft (€14–22) (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:fakanal: The restaurant with tables on the first floor of the Central Market: goulash, pork pörkölt with dumplings and other simple Hungarian dishes, served at tables with the market bustle below.
vp:fakanal: Goulash soup is around 3,100 Ft and pörkölt with dumplings about 5,100 Ft, i.e. €8–14 (October 2026 guide). Hours from guides, to be confirmed: closed on Sundays.
vd:szimply: A small, bright place for breakfast and brunch, between Deák Ferenc tér and Astoria: eggs cooked various ways, sourdough bread, vegetable dishes and good coffee. Handy to start the day in the centre.
vp:szimply: Breakfast with coffee is around 4,000–6,000 Ft (€11–16) (menu not seen). Hours from an October 2026 guide, to be confirmed: closed on Sundays and the kitchen closes about half an hour earlier.
vd:retro: A lángos kiosk a short walk from Parliament, with a few outdoor tables: the classic fried flatbread with sour cream and cheese, or with ham, sausage or vegetables. The city's most typical quick lunch.
vp:retro: A lángos costs about 3,490–5,990 Ft (€10–16) according to an October 2026 guide (menu not seen). Hours from a guide, to be confirmed.
vd:frici: A popular canteen (kifőzde) where students and locals eat: pörkölt, chicken paprikás, vegetable dishes and homemade desserts at low prices, in a simple two-floor room. Order the dish and choose a side separately.
vp:frici: Dishes cost about 900–3,600 Ft plus 400–450 Ft for the side (October 2026 guide, July 2026 prices): a full meal is under €10. Hours from a guide, to be confirmed: closed on Sundays and the kitchen may close as early as 8pm.
vd:disznotoros: A butcher's with a kitchen a few steps from Deák Ferenc tér: sausages, black pudding, roast legs and ribs, with sides like cabbage and pickled cucumbers. Choose at the counter, pay by weight and eat standing up or at little tables.
vp:disznotoros: A plate with three sausages and a side is around 3,000–4,000 Ft (€8–11) (October 2026 guide). Hours from a guide, to be confirmed.
vd:bors: A small bar for soups and hot baguettes in the Jewish quarter, with a queue on the pavement at lunchtime: the menu changes every day, with creative soups and filled baguettes. Few seats, mostly standing.
vp:bors: A soup costs about 2,060 Ft and a baguette about 4,120 Ft (€6–11) according to an October 2026 guide. Hours from a guide, to be confirmed.
cd:stefanocupola: Go up by lift and on foot to the dome: a 360-degree view over the city.
cd:szepmuveszeti: El Greco, Goya and Raphael in the large neoclassical building on Heroes' Square.
cd:nemzeti: Hungarian art from the Middle Ages to the 20th century, in Buda Castle.
cd:terror: The museum in the former headquarters of the fascist and communist secret police, on Andrássy út.
cd:gellertbagni: The Art Nouveau baths by the Danube: pools with columns and mosaics.
cx:gellertbagni: The price changes at weekends and with a cabin or a locker.
cd:rudas: 16th-century Turkish baths and a rooftop pool overlooking the Danube.
cd:labirinto: Tunnels under Castle Hill, mixing history and Dracula tales.
cd:opera: The neo-Renaissance theatre with marble stairs and a gilded auditorium, with a guided tour.
cd:dunacruise: An hour on the Danube below Parliament and the Castle.
cd:zoobud: The early 20th-century zoo next to the Széchenyi baths.
cd:nemzetimuz: Hungarian history in a neoclassical building with a grand staircase.
